purpose: Finite, inert negative source/run evidence fixtures for the #846 Agent Bridge package-staging acceptance predicates. Each fixture is a complete literal evidence record that the acceptance gate must reject for exactly one named reason. No fixture is a real run, and no fixture establishes any staging evidence.

inertness.note: Every value in this file is a literal. There are no ranges, repeat counts, wildcards, templates, format strings or environment references to expand, so the record set is finite by construction. The file is data only; nothing here is executed, contacted or applied to a real environment.

rejection_contract.note: A fixture is valid test data only when the gate rejects it and names the documented reason. A synthetic rejection cannot satisfy any actual Windows staging case.

fixtures.defect: The record declares an evidence schema version this acceptance suite does not implement, so none of its field meanings can be trusted.
The record is filed under a different work-unit id than #846, so its reconciliation counts cannot answer the #846 denominator obligation.
The record binds its source proof to a path outside the #846 exclusive mutable scope, so the staging source it claims to describe is not the subject of this acceptance suite.

The recorded blob digest is the SHA-256 of empty input and therefore does not match the current package_staging.rs bytes; the evidence was produced against a different (or unrecorded) source revision.
The run record selected zero Agent Bridge staging tests, so it establishes no staging evidence at all.
The run record claims a nine-test denominator that is not the eleven-function set the issue requires, so the recorded pass cannot reconcile the historical baseline.
The run record omits AGENT_BRIDGE_FAIL_DESTINATION_EXISTS, so one of the two separately asserted post-create fault subcases was never run even though the function count looks complete.
The run record reports passed with zero executed assertions, which is exactly the assertion-free success the issue forbids for an unavailable Agent Bridge fixture.
The environment record does not record the privilege facts, so the reader cannot tell ready environment from missing privilege.
The privileged staging cases are marked required while the record simultaneously reports that no supported environment provided them; missing setup must stay incomplete, never a simulated pass.
The privileged case names no D-INT environment owner, so an irreducibly privileged scenario has no exact accountable owner.
The privileged case names an owner outside the documented D-INT environment ownership set, so the scenario has no exact owner.
The privileged run carries no Windows identity, runner or elevation provenance, so it cannot be an actual current privileged run.
Cleanup failed while the record still reports passed, which would turn a cleanup failure into an environment-unavailable success.
Cleanup disposition is unknown, so the record cannot be a passing staging result; unknown external effect is not success.
The record leaves a fixture-owned temporary directory behind and still reports passed, so owned fixture objects were not cleaned.
The record claims an unrelated parent object as fixture-owned cleanup, which would authorise deleting an object the fixture never owned.
The protected ProgramData contour is replaced by an arbitrary writable temp root, which substitutes the protected installation contour and is never valid OS ACL evidence.
The fixture setup is recorded as an unsupported/privateless disposition while the record still reports passed, which is the unavailable-then-Ok path the issue forbids.
The ProtectedRootLease open was never verified yet the record claims a ready fixture and a pass, so lease-open failure became invisible.
The package run is red but the record lists no separately owned failures, so a failing run would read as an unowned green result.
The diff includes Cargo.toml, which is outside the test-only exclusive mutable scope for #846 and is forbidden by the issue.
The diff still carries the retired .github/temporary/work-unit-846.md reservation marker; a reservation merge is never test evidence.
A package test result is relabelled ProductProof, which the support and status contract forbids without Product Proof.
A package test result is relabelled installation support, which the issue explicitly says this work unit does not prove.
The record claims Clippy passed only because broad suppression was applied, which is not an acceptable package Clippy proof.
